title: A short regex can take longer than the age of the universe
body: Backtracking regex engines try possibilities one by one; nested quantifiers like (a+)+ multiply those possibilities exponentially on near-miss input. The string fails only after the engine explores a combinatorial maze. This is why one user-supplied pattern has taken down large sites, and why linear-time engines like RE2 refuse backreferences.
source_hint: Cox, 'Regular Expression Matching Can Be Simple and Fast' (2007)
